findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a series label, not a hook, so the actual hook is buried in sentence two.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of DOCKER IMAGES: LAYERS, CACHE, LEAN BUILDS. Your 1.1GB Node image and your cache miss on every single push are the same bug: you put the thing that changes most at the bottom of the stack."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and move the part label to the end: "Your 1.1GB Node image and your cache miss on every single push are the same bug: you put the thing that changes most at the bottom of the stack. ... (Part 2 of DOCKER IMAGES: LAYERS, CACHE, LEAN BUILDS.)"

findings.summary: Page 1's sections run 6 → 7 → 8 → 1, so the part opens with the recap/cheat-sheet material and only reaches its section 1 at the bottom of the page.
findings.evidence: Block order on page 1: "6. What Each Command Tells You", "7. CI Cache Line", "8. Seven Rules Recap", callout "A Stack Of Diffs", then "1. Diagnose By Symptom".
findings.fix: Move the "1. Diagnose By Symptom" table to the top of page 1, ahead of the command table, and renumber the remaining page-1 sections so they ascend from it; keep the "A Stack Of Diffs" takeaway callout as the last block on the page.

findings.summary: Heading "3. Quick Q" already appears on page 2.
findings.fix: Rename this section, or merge it with the earlier one.

findings.summary: Page 2 opens with "7. Mental Model" — a closing summary numbered out of sequence and duplicating page 1's section 7 — before the sections 2–6 it is meant to summarize.
findings.evidence: Page 2 block order: "7. Mental Model" (flow diagram "rarely changes: base / sometimes: deps / often: source / never ships: builder stage"), then "2. Quick Q", "3. Quick Q", "4. Numbers Worth Memorising", "5. Pre-Push Checklist", "6. One-Minute Audit"; page 1 already uses "7. CI Cache Line".
findings.fix: Move the Mental Model diagram to the end of page 2, directly above the "Control The Churn" callout it illustrates, and renumber it to follow "6. One-Minute Audit" so section numbers are unique and ascending across both pages.

findings.summary: The caption's page count is wrong and names the wrong closing page for the handbook.
findings.evidence: caption: "Ten pages, ending at 150MB with a non-root user and pinned digests." — the handbook is 16 pages (part 01 has 11 `page_title` entries, part 02 has 2, part 03 has 3), and part 01's last page is "Alpine vs Slim vs Distroless vs Scratch", not the 150MB page.
findings.fix: Replace with an accurate closing line, e.g. "Sixteen pages across three parts: 1.1GB down to 150MB non-root, then base-image choice, secrets and safe pinning."

findings.summary: #kubernetes names an orchestration technology this part never touches — the pages cover only image layers, build cache, inspection commands and pre-push hygiene.
findings.evidence: hashtags include "#kubernetes"; page titles are "Inspection Tools, CI Cache & Symptom Table" and "Quick Q&A, Size Numbers & Pre-Push Audit", and no block mentions Kubernetes, pods or orchestration
findings.fix: Replace #kubernetes with a tag that matches the content, e.g. #multistagebuild or #dockerimages.

findings.summary: The registry-cache recipe omits that the default `docker` driver cannot export cache, so the `--cache-to` line fails out of the box in CI.
findings.evidence: sidebox "buildx Registry Cache": "`--cache-from type=registry,ref=repo/app:cache`" / "`--cache-to ...,mode=max` exports intermediate stages" — Docker's registry-cache docs state "This cache storage backend works with the default `docker` driver only when the containerd image store is enabled. If the containerd image store isn't enabled, use a different driver."
findings.fix: Add a line to the sidebox: "needs a `docker-container` builder (`docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container`) or the containerd image store — the default docker driver errors with `Cache export is not supported for the docker driver`."

findings.summary: The heading promises seven rules but the recap bullets do not contain seven rules.
findings.evidence: "8. Seven Rules Recap" followed by a five-item bullets block whose items bundle roughly ten distinct rules ("Order by change frequency; manifests before source", "Clean in the same RUN; ship artifacts via multi-stage", "Ignore aggressively; pin base digests; never run as root", "Commit lockfiles; `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for determinism", plus the inline-cache bullet).
findings.fix: Either split the bullets into exactly seven one-rule items, or retitle the heading to "Rules Recap" so it makes no count claim.

findings.summary: A local single-stage debugging recipe sits inside the CI-cache sidebox, where it does not belong to the section's topic.
findings.evidence: Under heading "7. CI Cache Line", sidebox "buildx Registry Cache" contains "`docker build --target <stage> -t dbg . && docker run --rm -it dbg sh` to poke a stage" alongside `--cache-from`/`--cache-to` items.
findings.fix: Move the `--target` debug one-liner out of the CI cache sidebox into the "One-Minute Audit"/inspection section, leaving the sidebox to cache-from, cache-to mode=max, and the weekly `--no-cache --pull` rebuild.

findings.summary: The "Ans:" answer labels under both Quick Q questions render at a tiny, near-illegible size compared with surrounding body text.
findings.evidence: The marker reading "Ans:--" appears twice (under "Why did the image not shrink after I added rm -rf /var/cache?" and under "Same Dockerfile, but CI rebuilds everything every run. Why?") at roughly a third of the body text height, collapsing into an unreadable smudge.
findings.fix: Raise the answer-label font size to at least the body text size (or drop the label entirely, since the bulleted answer already follows the question).

findings.summary: Two different sections are both numbered 6 and present the same four inspection commands, so the audit recipe re-teaches page 1's table as if new.
findings.evidence: Page 1 "6. What Each Command Tells You" table lists docker history --no-trunc / dive / docker system df / build --progress=plain; page 2 "6. One-Minute Audit" code block lists "docker build --progress=plain .", "docker history --no-trunc img", "docker system df", "dive img".
findings.fix: Renumber the audit section so no two sections share a number, and reframe it explicitly as the run-order of the commands already tabled (e.g. title it "Audit Order" and drop the repeated per-command gloss comments).
